title: The Valley of Dry Bones and Two Sticks Combined

questions.question: Where did the Spirit of the Lord set Ezekiel down in a vision, and what was it full of?
options: In the middle of a valley; it was full of bones
On top of a mountain; it was full of eagles
Near the river Chebar; it was full of mud
In a great city; it was full of statues of gold
questions.correctAnswer: In the middle of a valley; it was full of bones
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 37:1 (ESV): "The hand of the Lord was upon me, and he brought me out in the Spirit of the Lord and set me down in the middle of the valley; it was full of bones."

questions.question: What condition were the bones in as Ezekiel was led back and forth among them?
options: They were very many on the surface of the valley, and behold, they were very dry
They were charred by fire and broken
They were covered with a thin layer of dust
They were mostly skulls and hands
questions.correctAnswer: They were very many on the surface of the valley, and behold, they were very dry
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 37:2 (ESV): "He led me around among them, and behold, there were very many on the surface of the valley, and behold, they were very dry."

questions.question: What question did God ask Ezekiel concerning the bones, and how did Ezekiel reply?
options: God: "Can these bones live?" Ezekiel: "O Lord God, you know."
God: "Whose bones are these?" Ezekiel: "They are the kings of Judah."
God: "Will they ever see the light of day?" Ezekiel: "Only if you command it."
God: "Why are these bones dry?" Ezekiel: "Because of our sins."
questions.correctAnswer: God: "Can these bones live?" Ezekiel: "O Lord God, you know."
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 37:3 (ESV): "And he said to me, 'Son of man, can these bones live?' And I answered, 'O Lord God, you know.'"

questions.question: What was Ezekiel commanded to prophesy over the dry bones first?
options: "O dry bones, hear the word of the Lord. Thus says the Lord God to these bones: Behold, I will cause breath to enter you, and you shall live."
"Arise from the dust and take up your swords."
"Be gathered together and form a great wall."
"Rain shall fall and wash away your dust."
questions.correctAnswer: "O dry bones, hear the word of the Lord. Thus says the Lord God to these bones: Behold, I will cause breath to enter you, and you shall live."
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 37:4-5 (ESV): "Then he said to me, 'Prophesy over these bones, and say to them, O dry bones, hear the word of the Lord. Thus says the Lord God to these bones: Behold, I will cause breath to enter you, and you shall live.'"

questions.question: When Ezekiel prophesied as commanded, what noise and movement occurred?
options: There was a sound, and behold, a rattling, and the bones came together, bone to its bone
A great earthquake shook the valley, and the bones stood upright
A loud trumpet sounded from heaven, and fire fell on the bones
A mighty wind swept through and blew the bones into heaps
questions.correctAnswer: There was a sound, and behold, a rattling, and the bones came together, bone to its bone
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 37:7 (ESV): "So I prophesied as I was commanded. And as I prophesied, there was a sound, and behold, a rattling, and the bones came together, bone to its bone."

questions.question: After the sinews, flesh, and skin covered the bones, what was still lacking?
options: There was no breath in them
They had no eyes to see
They could not walk
Their hands were empty of weapons
questions.correctAnswer: There was no breath in them
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 37:8 (ESV): "And I looked, and behold, there were sinews on them, and flesh had come upon them, and skin had covered them. But there was no breath in them."

questions.question: Who/what was Ezekiel told to prophesy to next, to put breath into the slain?
options: The breath (or wind/Spirit) from the four winds
The Angel of the Lord
The clouds of heaven
The fire of the altar
questions.correctAnswer: The breath (or wind/Spirit) from the four winds
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 37:9 (ESV): "Then he said to me, 'Prophesy to the breath; prophesy, son of man, and say to the breath, Thus says the Lord God: Come from the four winds, O breath, and breathe on these slain, that they may live.'"

questions.question: When Ezekiel prophesied to the breath, what happened to the slain?
options: The breath came into them, and they lived and stood on their feet, an exceedingly great army
They arose and began to sing a lamentation
They awoke but remained lying in the valley
They immediately scattered to the mountains
questions.correctAnswer: The breath came into them, and they lived and stood on their feet, an exceedingly great army
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 37:10 (ESV): "So I prophesied as he commanded me, and the breath came into them, and they lived and stood on their feet, an exceedingly great army."

questions.question: Who do the dry bones represent, according to God?
options: The whole house of Israel
The armies of Babylon
The righteous dead of all nations
The false prophets of Judah
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 37:11 (ESV): "Then he said to me, 'Son of man, these bones are the whole house of Israel.'"

questions.question: What were the people of Israel saying about their situation (which the dry bones represented)?
options: "Our bones are dried up, and our hope is lost; we are indeed cut off."
"We are like grass that withers in the sun."
"God has given us a new life in Babylon."
"The temple is destroyed, but our hearts remain firm."
questions.correctAnswer: "Our bones are dried up, and our hope is lost; we are indeed cut off."
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 37:11 (ESV): "Behold, they say, 'Our bones are dried up, and our hope is lost; we are indeed cut off.'"

questions.question: To illustrate the future of Israel, Ezekiel is told to take two sticks. What was he to write on the first stick?
options: "For Judah, and the people of Israel associated with him"
"For Levi and the priesthood"
"For David and his descendants"
"For Jerusalem, the holy city"
questions.correctAnswer: "For Judah, and the people of Israel associated with him"
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 37:16 (ESV): "Son of man, take a stick and write on it, 'For Judah, and the people of Israel associated with him'"

questions.question: What was Ezekiel to write on the second stick?
options: "For Joseph (the stick of Ephraim) and all the house of Israel associated with him"
"For Benjamin, the beloved of the Lord"
"For Samaria, the rebellious city"
"For the ten lost tribes of the north"
questions.correctAnswer: "For Joseph (the stick of Ephraim) and all the house of Israel associated with him"
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 37:16 (ESV): "...then take another stick and write on it, 'For Joseph (the stick of Ephraim) and all the house of Israel associated with him.'"

questions.question: What was Ezekiel to do with the two sticks?
options: Join them into one stick, that they may become one in his hand
Burn them on an altar
Plant them in the ground to grow as trees
Break them both before the people
questions.correctAnswer: Join them into one stick, that they may become one in his hand
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 37:17 (ESV): "And join them one to another into one stick, that they may become one in your hand."

questions.question: What does the joining of the two sticks mean?
options: God will make them one nation in the land... and they shall be no longer two nations, and no longer divided into two kingdoms
Judah and Egypt will make a treaty
The wood of the cross will unite Jews and Gentiles
The exiles of Babylon will merge with the local population
questions.correctAnswer: God will make them one nation in the land... and they shall be no longer two nations, and no longer divided into two kingdoms
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 37:22 (ESV): "And I will make them one nation in the land, on the mountains of Israel... and they shall be no longer two nations, and no longer divided into two kingdoms."

questions.question: Who does God promise will be king over this reunited, cleansed nation?
options: My servant David shall be king over them, and they shall all have one shepherd
A prophet from the line of Samuel
A righteous priest from the line of Zadok
They shall have no king but the Lord Himself directly
questions.correctAnswer: My servant David shall be king over them, and they shall all have one shepherd
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 37:24 (ESV): "My servant David shall be king over them, and they shall all have one shepherd."

key_verse_text: "My dwelling place shall be with them, and I will be their God, and they shall be my people."
